title: pm-dispatch model tiering: a card whose surface touches `docs/adr/**` is dispatched at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER with effort xhigh, no one-line exit
body:
Filing gate: ③ a task ordered directly by the project owner, quoted verbatim below.
Reader: `domain:skills` seat, next PR on `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.data.mjs` (`MANDATORY_TIER_GLOB_ROWS`) plus the PM skill text that states the tiering policy.
Dedupe (open AND closed): "ADR drafting cards must be dispatched at the fable model tier mandatory tier glob docs/adr" → 11 hits, none about an ADR tier mandate (nearest: #7945, the spec-semantic tier mandate, and #17950, governed-surface tiering, both closed completed); "dispatch effort xhigh floor per surface, model tier mandate MANDATORY_TIER_GLOB_ROWS new row" → 0 hits.

## The order

田騏 (`marchtian`), 2026-10-25T01:40:25Z, in the project thread that drafted #25403, verbatim and untranslated:

> adr 这种任务都需要 fable extra，重新处理并立skills 卡片

Read as: "fable" = the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` constant in `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` (the claim template spells the constant, never a model id); "extra" = `effort: xhigh`, the claim template's word for extra-high effort (`Container & model` line of the SKILL.md claim template); "这种任务" = every card whose deliverable is ADR text, i.e. whose file surface touches `docs/adr/**`. 「都需要」 = no exemption.

## Why

An ADR is what later cards are cut from (AGENTS.md Prime Directive 13: an accepted ADR binds until a superseding one says otherwise), and `docs/adr/**` lands only by the maintainer's hand (Tier H). A drafting error is paid twice: once by the maintainer reading it, and again by every implementation card built on it. The order puts ADR drafting at the top tier and effort.

The case that triggered it: #25403 (the inter-app dependency ADR) was claimed with `model: default tier (dispatch-gates --tier: "no path-derived mandate", floor sonnet · default opus · ceiling fable)` and `effort: high` (claim comment 6390714959), and draft PR #25717 was written at that tier. Nothing mechanical could have said otherwise: measured at `origin/main` `43edf90b`, `MANDATORY_TIER_GLOB_ROWS` holds three globs (`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md`, `.claude/agents/os-dev.md`, `skills/**`), and `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --tier docs/adr/0028-metadata-naming-and-namespace-isolation.md` answers "Model tier — no path-derived mandate: the surface hits none of the 3 declared glob(s)". #25717 is being re-drafted at the ordered tier.

## What to change

1. **The tier row.** `MANDATORY_TIER_GLOB_ROWS` in `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.data.mjs` gains `glob: 'docs/adr/**'`, `tier: 'CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER'`, a `why:` quoting the order, and `oneLineExit: false` — 「都需要」 closes the one-line mechanical-edit exit by path, the same shape the `skills/**` row has. The table's existing self-test guards (the glob names an existing path; no two globs disagree on a tier) cover the new row.
2. **The effort floor.** The table carries a tier and nothing else, while the order also fixes effort at `xhigh`. Either the row gains an effort floor that `--tier` prints beside the tier, or the PM skill states the floor where the claim's `effort:` word is chosen (`references/execution-duties.md` dispatch section, and the `effort: <medium | high | xhigh | max,按卡难度定>` slot of the SKILL.md claim template). Whichever carrier is chosen, `xhigh` is a floor that "按卡难度" can raise to `max` and ⛔ never lower.
3. **The policy text.** The table's header says it is a machine-readable copy of one predicate from the PM skill's tiering policy, and that the skill wins when they disagree. The skill text that states that policy gains this order as a clause in the same edit, so the table stays a copy.
4. ⚠ `references/instrument-discipline.md` freezes `dispatch-gates.mjs` against new derivation lines. Item 1 is a data row in an existing table; a printed effort line (item 2, first option) may count as a new line. The PR says which side of that freeze its choice falls on.

## Boundary

- This changes PM-lane rules: `.claude/**` is a governed surface (Tier S), `scripts/pm/**` outside the gate scripts is the `domain:skills` lane's. Whether this order is enough to land a tiering change, or the maintainer's word is owed, is triage's and the director seat's call; ⛔ this card does not decide it.
- Not in scope: re-dispatching ADR cards that already merged.
